source_refs.note: 3- Termination Phase: a main subheading of Activation of Amino Acids and the Phases of Translation, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 140-140.

blocks.text: When a stop codon is exposed at A site, no aminoacyl-tRNA comes to A-site (because there is no anticodon of the stop codons). Stop codon at A site is recognized by a protein called release factor. It releases the polypeptide from the tRNA present at P site. In this way, the process of translation is terminated. The tRNA is also released from ribosome and ribosomal subunits separate from the mRNA.

blocks.alt: Left: the ribosome with a tRNA (anticodon ACC) on UGG in the P site carrying the chain Met-Leu-Ser-Trp and the stop codon UAA in the A site; a release factor approaches. Middle: the release factor sits in the A site and the polypeptide is freed from the tRNA. Below: the polypeptide, the larger subunit, the smaller subunit, the tRNA and the release factor separate from the mRNA.
blocks.caption: Figure 19.20: Termination phase of translation (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 19.20).
